title: A well-ordered union of submodules with successive quotients of projective dimension at most n has projective dimension at most n
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ an integer and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $(E,\le)$ be a well-ordered set (a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element) and $(M_e)_{e\in E}$ a family of $R$-submodules of $M$ such that $M_{e'}\subseteq M_e$ whenever $e'\le e$, and $M=\bigcup_{e\in E}M_e$. For $e\in E$ let $M_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}M_{e'}$ (the union of a chain of submodules, hence a submodule of $M_e$; it is $0$ when $e$ is the least element of $E$). Assume that for every $e\in E$ the quotient module $M_e/M_{<e}$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], i.e. an exact sequence $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\to M_e/M_{<e}\to0$ with every $P_i$ a projective $R$-module. Then $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800; argument of Auslander)

proof.text: (The inductive claim.) Following the source we prove by induction on $n\ge0$ the claim $C(n)$: for every $R$-module $M$, every well-ordered set $(E,\le)$ and every family $(M_e)_{e\in E}$ of submodules with $M_{e'}\subseteq M_e$ for $e'\le e$ and $M=\bigcup_eM_e$ such that every $M_e/M_{<e}$ ($M_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}M_{e'}$) has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], the module $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$. The item is $C(n)$. Two facts about chains used below: since $E$ is totally ordered, the $M_e$ form a chain, so $M_{<e}$ is a submodule of $M_e$, and finitely many elements of $M$ (resp. of $M_{<e}$) lie in a single $M_{e_0}$ (resp. a single $M_{e'}$ with $e'<e$): each lies in some $M_{e_j}$ and one takes the largest $e_j$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, line 26808 ('We will prove this by induction on n')

proof.text: (Case $n=0$: the quotients are projective and the projections split.) For $n=0$ a projective resolution of length $\le0$ of $Q_e=M_e/M_{<e}$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] is an exact sequence $0\to P_0\to Q_e\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], i.e. an isomorphism $P_0\cong Q_e$ with $P_0$ projective; hence $Q_e$ is projective [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand] (2). The sequence $0\to M_{<e}\to M_e\xrightarrow{q_e}Q_e\to0$ ($q_e$ the quotient map, surjective with kernel $M_{<e}$) is short exact with projective quotient, so there is an $R$-linear section $s_e:Q_e\to M_e$ with $q_e\circ s_e=\mathrm{id}_{Q_e}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ses-projective-quotient-splits]. Choose one $s_e$ for every $e\in E$ (axiom of choice), regard it as a map to $M$, and let $\psi:\bigoplus_{e\in E}Q_e\to M$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] be the $R$-linear map $\psi((x_e)_e)=\sum_es_e(x_e)$ (a finite sum).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26811-26813

proof.text:
($\psi$ is injective.) Let $x=(x_e)_e
e0$ in $ igoplus_eQ_e$. Its support $\{e:x_e
e0\}$ is finite and nonempty; let $e_{\max}$ be its largest element. For $e$ in the support, $s_e(x_e)\in M_e\subseteq M_{e_{\max}}$, so $y=\psi(x)\in M_{e_{\max}}$. Apply $q_{e_{\max}}$: for $e<e_{\max}$ in the support, $s_e(x_e)\in M_e\subseteq M_{<e_{\max}}=\operatorname{Ker}q_{e_{\max}}$, and $q_{e_{\max}}(s_{e_{\max}}(x_{e_{\max}}))=x_{e_{\max}}$. Hence $q_{e_{\max}}(y)=x_{e_{\max}}

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26813-26817

proof.text: ($\psi$ is surjective, by transfinite induction.) Suppose not. Since $M=\bigcup_eM_e$, the set of $e\in E$ with $M_e\not\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$ is nonempty; as $E$ is well-ordered it has a least element $e$, so $M_{e'}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$ for every $e'<e$, hence $M_{<e}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$. Take $y\in M_e\setminus\operatorname{Im}\psi$ and $x_e=q_e(y)\in Q_e$. Then $q_e(y-s_e(x_e))=x_e-x_e=0$, so $y-s_e(x_e)\in M_{<e}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$, and $s_e(x_e)=\psi(\iota_e(x_e))\in\operatorname{Im}\psi$ ($\iota_e$ the canonical inclusion). So $y\in\operatorname{Im}\psi$, a contradiction. Thus $\psi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26818-26824

proof.text: (Conclusion for $n=0$.) $\bigoplus_eQ_e$ is projective as a direct sum of the projective modules $Q_e$ [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-sum-family] (Stacks 065Q, which the source cites), so $M\cong\bigoplus_eQ_e$ is projective [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand] (2), and $0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0$ is a projective resolution of length $\le0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. This is $C(0)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26824-26826

proof.text: (Case $n\ge1$: the free modules.) Assume $C(n-1)$ and let $M,E,(M_e)$ be as in $C(n)$. Let $F=\bigoplus_{m\in M}R$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] be the free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis $([m])_{m\in M}$, and $\pi:F\to M$ the $R$-linear map with $\pi([m])=m$; it is surjective. Let $K=\operatorname{Ker}\pi$. For $e\in E$ let $F_e\subseteq F$ be the submodule spanned by $\{[m]:m\in M_e\}$ (free on the set of elements of $M_e$) and $K_e=K\cap F_e=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi|_{F_e}:F_e\to M_e)$; $\pi(F_e)=M_e$. For $e'\le e$, $M_{e'}\subseteq M_e$ gives $F_{e'}\subseteq F_e$ and $K_{e'}\subseteq K_e$ (the transition maps are injective). Every element of $F$ is a finite combination of basis vectors $[m_j]$, and the $m_j$ lie in one $M_{e_0}$ (Step 1), so $F=\bigcup_eF_e$ and $K=\bigcup_eK_e$. Put $F_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}F_{e'}$ and $K_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}K_{e'}$. By the chain fact of Step 1, $F_{<e}$ is the span of $\{[m]:m\in M_{<e}\}$ (an element of the span uses finitely many $m_j\in M_{<e}$, all in one $M_{e'}$, $e'<e$), and $K_{<e}=K\cap F_{<e}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26829-26837

proof.text: (The short exact sequence of successive quotients.) The inclusion $K_e\subseteq F_e$ and $\pi|_{F_e}$ induce $R$-linear maps $\alpha:K_e/K_{<e}\to F_e/F_{<e}$ and $\beta:F_e/F_{<e}\to M_e/M_{<e}$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] (well defined since $K_{<e}\subseteq F_{<e}$ and $\pi(F_{<e})\subseteq M_{<e}$, Step 6). The sequence $0\to K_e/K_{<e}\xrightarrow{\alpha}F_e/F_{<e}\xrightarrow{\beta}M_e/M_{<e}\to0$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: $\alpha$ injective, since $k\in K_e\cap F_{<e}$ lies in $K\cap F_{<e}=K_{<e}$; $\beta\alpha=0$ since $\pi(K_e)=0$; $\operatorname{Ker}\beta\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\alpha$: if $f\in F_e$ and $m:=\pi(f)\in M_{<e}$, then $[m]\in F_{<e}\subseteq F_e$ and $f-[m]\in F_e$ with $\pi(f-[m])=0$, so $f-[m]\in K_e$ and $f\bmod F_{<e}=\alpha((f-[m])\bmod K_{<e})$; $\beta$ surjective since $\pi(F_e)=M_e$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26837-26844

proof.text: ($F_e/F_{<e}$ is free, hence has a projective resolution of length $\le n-1$.) The basis $\{[m]:m\in M_e\}$ of $F_e$ is the disjoint union of $\{[m]:m\in M_{<e}\}$, a basis of $F_{<e}$ (Step 6), and $B_e=\{[m]:m\in M_e\setminus M_{<e}\}$; so $F_e=F_{<e}\oplus\operatorname{span}(B_e)$ and $F_e/F_{<e}$ is free with basis the classes of $B_e$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] (as the source says), hence projective [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. So $0\to F_e/F_{<e}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}F_e/F_{<e}\to0$ is a projective resolution of length $\le0$, and padding with zeros [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-well-defined] (1) gives one of length $\le n-1$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] ($n-1\ge0$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26844-26846

proof.text: (Dimension shifting.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ses-kernel] (Stacks 065S (1), which the source cites) with $m=n-1$ to the short exact sequence of Step 7: the middle term $F_e/F_{<e}$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n-1$ (Step 8), and the quotient $M_e/M_{<e}$ has one of length $\le n$ by hypothesis. Hence $K_e/K_{<e}$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n-1$, for every $e\in E$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26847-26850

proof.text: (Induction hypothesis.) By Steps 6 and 9, the module $K$, the well-ordered set $E$ and the submodules $(K_e)_{e\in E}$ satisfy the hypotheses of $C(n-1)$: $K_{e'}\subseteq K_e$ for $e'\le e$, $K=\bigcup_eK_e$, $K_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}K_{e'}$, and every $K_e/K_{<e}$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n-1$. By $C(n-1)$ there is an exact sequence $0\to Q_{n-1}\to\dots\to Q_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}K\to0$ with all $Q_i$ projective [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26850-26851

proof.text: (Splicing: conclusion for $n$.) Let $j:K\to F$ be the inclusion. The sequence $0\to Q_{n-1}\to\dots\to Q_1\to Q_0\xrightarrow{j\varepsilon}F\xrightarrow{\pi}M\to0$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: at $M$, $\pi$ is surjective; at $F$, $\operatorname{Im}(j\varepsilon)=K=\operatorname{Ker}\pi$ since $\varepsilon$ is surjective; at $Q_0$, $\operatorname{Ker}(j\varepsilon)=\operatorname{Ker}\varepsilon$ since $j$ is injective, which is the image of $Q_1\to Q_0$ (for $n=1$, $\varepsilon$ is injective and $Q_0$ is the leftmost term); at $Q_1,\dots,Q_{n-1}$ exactness is that of the resolution of $K$. $F$ is free, hence projective [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. So this is a projective resolution of $M$ of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], which proves $C(n)$ and the lemma.
